robot-dog.title: Robot Dog
robot-dog.summary: Quadrupedal robot designed in CAD with a small team. Inverse kinematics maps three degrees of freedom per leg to six degrees of freedom at the body.
captions: Quadrupedal robot, designed in CAD with a small team. Several leg geometries were modeled before settling on a simple linkage.
Inverse kinematics maps the three degrees of freedom in each leg to full six-degree-of-freedom control of the body.
The same solver commands the body through arbitrary poses while the feet stay planted.
Head on, the roll and side-to-side sway of the body are easier to see.
Walking gait, with the camera tracking the robot across the mat.

pid-seesaw.title: PID Seesaw
pid-seesaw.summary: Ball-balancing beam. An infrared distance sensor reports the ball's position, and a servo and linkage tilt the beam under PID control.
captions: Ball-balancing beam. An infrared distance sensor measures the ball's position, and a servo drives the beam through a linkage.

A PID controller holds the ball at center and rejects disturbances. The second revision upgraded the hardware and corrected the control law: setting the servo angle to the controller output, rather than adding the output to the angle, removed an unintended integrator and the lag it caused.

media.caption: The first version, built from LEGO.
The LEGO version wired to an Arduino.
The wooden version recovering after the ball is pushed.

micromanipulator.title: Micromanipulator
micromanipulator.tag: Closed-loop stepper control, 100 nm theoretical resolution
micromanipulator.summary: A low-cost, 3D-printed alternative to industrial micromanipulators, which cost $1,000 to $60,000. Geometric microstepping accounts for the true 45° phase spacing of the motor's coils, where the standard formula assumes 90°. A row of 17 axially magnetized magnets forms a locally rotating field that increases encoder resolution 8.5 times over a single diametric magnet. Angular error fell from about 0.08° in open loop to 0.0045° with closed-loop control, and about 0.0005° with PID control in C++, which allows a theoretical end-effector resolution of 100 nm. Physical testing of that resolution is the next step.
captions: A low-cost, 3D-printed micromanipulator. Three NEMA 17 stepper motors turn horns that move the end effector through parallel brass rods on ball joints, in place of industrial units that cost $1,000 to $60,000.

Geometric microstepping accounts for the true 45° phase spacing of the motor's coils, and a row of 17 axially magnetized magnets raises encoder resolution 8.5 times. Angular error fell from about 0.08° in open loop to 0.0005° with PID control, for a theoretical end-effector resolution of 100 nm.

media.caption: Traditional and geometric microstepping: phase currents, field angle, and magnetic angle error.

ship-in-a-bottle.title: Ship in a Bottle
ship-in-a-bottle.summary: A ship built from scratch and assembled inside the bottle. The work demanded extreme precision and custom tools made from clothes hangers to reach inside.

media.caption: The build: shaping and carving the hull, painting, rigging the masts and sails, then passing the folded ship through the neck and raising it inside the bottle.
Finished ship in its bottle.

chess-engine.title: Chess Engine
chess-engine.summary: A chess engine built on a bitboard representation and minimax search, later extended with iterative deepening and NNUE evaluation, which replaces handcrafted heuristics with a neural network. Rated 2000+ Elo against other bots on Lichess.

media.caption: The engine playing a game.
Minimax search over a game tree.
Engine source.

hybrid-networks.title: EvoGrad
hybrid-networks.tag: Hybrid neural networks: NEAT with gradient descent
hybrid-networks.summary: A neural network library that re-implements NEAT from its original paper and combines it with gradient descent. Evolution searches over network structure while gradient descent tunes the weights, producing compact, expressive networks suited to engineering and physics problems.

media.caption: Network evolved for XOR.

tennis-simulation.title: Tennis Statistics Library
tennis-simulation.summary: A library that simulates tennis matches from simple inputs, updated during play with Bayesian statistics. Monte Carlo simulation produces point importance and win probability.

media.caption: Win probability through a match, static compared with Bayesian updates.
Point importance during one match.

protein-classifier.title: Alzheimer's Protein Classifier
protein-classifier.summary: A support vector machine over genomic and proteomic data that classifies whether a protein sequence is associated with Alzheimer's disease, with controls to correct for sequence length bias. Accuracy: 80.3%.

media.caption: Research poster.
Sequence length analysis in the project notebook.

world-models.title: Plan Shallow While You Learn
world-models.summary: Co-authored paper accepted to the Continual World Models workshop at NeurIPS 2026 in Sydney. It shows that while a world model adapts to changed physics, planning compute should favor breadth over depth to maximize returns.

media.caption: Accepted to the Continual World Models workshop at NeurIPS 2026, Sydney, December 12. Photo of Sydney Harbour: Benh Lieu Song, CC BY-SA 4.0.
The workshop’s accepted papers include work co-authored by Yann LeCun and Fei-Fei Li.
Return against imagination depth, for a healthy model and three damping levels.
Return improvement from reallocating the same planning budget.
Deployment streams on the drag tiers.

asteroid-orbit.title: Orbit of Asteroid 1991 JF1
asteroid-orbit.summary: In a team of three, determined the orbit of asteroid 1991 JF1 from original observations: imaging over three nights, plate solving for celestial coordinates, and computing orbital elements with the Method of Gauss. Results were written up as a technical paper and submitted to the Minor Planet Center.

media.caption: Calibrated observation, with the asteroid circled.
Orbits of 6249 Jennifer and Earth in the ecliptic plane.
Photometric calibration against reference stars.
